newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition declines slightly in week.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition declines slightly in week.

text.p: The condition of the Texas wheat crop declined slightly during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.
"Dryland fields in the High Plains were in need of rain in the very near future to have any chance of a good crop. Irrigated fields were in good condition during the week," the report said.
Wheat was rated 11 percent excellent, 46 good, 36 fair, six poor and one very poor, versus last week's 18 percent excellent, 40 good, 36 fair, five poor and one very poor.
Three percent of the state's wheat acreage had headed, versus two percent last week and for the five-year average.
Across the Low Plains and north central Texas, fields were in good condition with some isolated rust problems.

Four percent of cotton acreage was planted, compared to seven percent last year and for the average. Corn acreage was 23 percent planted, versus 38 last year and 33 on average. Sorghum acreage was 19 percent planted, versus 31 last year and 29 percent for the average.
